question: The study of the multifunctional severity of COPD is performed with the BODEX and BODE indices, which have some common criteria. Which of the following criteria is exclusively part of one of the two indexes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "includes dyspnea assessment (MRC)" -> "not exclusive to BODEX" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODE index" -> "includes distance traveled (meters)" -> "not exclusive to BODE" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "includes body mass index (BMI)" -> "not exclusive to BODEX" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODE index" -> "includes forced vital capacity (FVC)" -> "not exclusive to BODE" -> 80%

CHAIN: "BODE index" -> "excludes dyspnea assessment (MRC)" -> "MRC is part of BODEX" -> 90%

CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "excludes body mass index (BMI)" -> "BMI is part of BODE" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The BODE and BODEX indices are both used to assess the severity of COPD, but they include different criteria. The BODE index includes forced vital capacity (FVC), while the BODEX index includes dyspnea assessment (MRC), distance traveled (meters), and body mass index (BMI). Therefore, the criteria that is exclusively part of one of the two indices is FVC, which is only included in the BODE index. The other criteria (dyspnea assessment, distance traveled, and BMI) are part of the BODEX index. Thus, the correct answer is that FVC is exclusive to the BODE index.
analysis: The BODE index includes four components: Body mass index (BMI), Obstruction (measured by FEV1), Dyspnea (assessed by the MRC scale), and Exercise capacity (measured by the 6-minute walk test). The BODEX index is similar but adds the presence of comorbidities. Among the options provided, 'Forced vital capacity (FVC)' is not a criterion in either index, while 'Distance traveled (meters)' refers to the exercise capacity component of the BODE index. 'Dyspnea assessment (MRC)' and 'Body mass index (BMI)' are common to both indices. Therefore, the criterion that is exclusively part of one of the two indices is 'Distance traveled (meters)', as it is specifically part of the BODE index and not the BODEX index, which focuses more on comorbidities. Thus, the best-supported option is 'Distance traveled (meters)'.
